architectural-decision-records.why: records the normalize-in-hash decision, the regenerated manifest, and the asset re-cut follow-up
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR 0058: normalize CRLF to LF before hashing at all three file-hash sites; regenerated the manifest sha; chose normalize-in-hash over eol=lf
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the fix ships a discrimination test proving CRLF and LF hash identically
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added a parity test: a CRLF script verifies against the LF-normalized manifest sha and so does its LF form; reverting to a raw-byte hash fails the CRLF case
quotes: replace each check with a no-op and require its test to fail

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the change alters hashing logic, so the test level is explicit
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: a unit-level parity fixture proves the line-ending invariant; the right level for a pure hashing change
quotes: Fast, isolated tests for logic; a smaller number of integration tests for the seams

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: coupling fires on the changed gate scripts; the behavior is pinned as a scenario
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: implements line-ending-stable hashing with a CRLF-and-LF discrimination scenario
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment. Every time this

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the sha256 is a tamper-detection integrity control over the gate scripts
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: normalization keeps the integrity property: a meaningful content change still changes the normalized hash, while a line-ending-only difference (a semantic no-op) is correctly treated as unchanged, so it does not weaken tamper detection
quotes: For the change in front of you, look up the matching sheet in the catalog below

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR states the limits rather than overclaiming
skeptical-audit.what: documented the lone-CR limitation, the UTF-8-text-only scope, and the required v1.1.0 asset re-cut, and verified all four regenerated hashes match
quotes: content hash, a query, a version/commit SHA, or a URL + retrieval date;

judge-arch.why: reviewed in fresh context before the PR
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context judge-arch over the three hash-site edits, the regenerated manifest, the test, and the ADR before opening the PR
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all

release-deployment-safety.why: a hashing fix; the v1.1.0 asset re-cut is noted as a follow-up in the ADR, not part of this diff
